newsitem.title: UK: Ldn platinum tense on Russia supplies, gold steady.
newsitem.headline: Ldn platinum tense on Russia supplies, gold steady.

text.p: The price of platinum had a rough ride on Friday as players, confused about a sudden squeeze in the metal, awaited word on delayed Russian supplies.
Prices eased almost $6.00 an ounce in nervous trades from their peak of $382.50 struck on Thursday amid rumours of difficulties surrounding a Russian swap deal with a Swiss bank.
But Russian officials subsequently denied any deal existed.
Gold fixed at $342.10 per ounce, just 10 cents up on its morning fix having been volatile earlier this week.
By 1500 GMT spot platinum was bid at $377.00 an ounce in London, down from an intraday high of $380.50.
Dealers said prices rose on rumours that a swap of 30 tonnes of Russian gold held by a Swiss bank as collateral against a hard currency loan for platinum and palladium might falter.
The market was already on tenterhooks after long delays in Russian PGM supplies due to bureaucratic snags.

Dealers said the latest squeeze was evident in the heavy Swiss borrowing of platinum that emerged on Thursday, sending the forward market into a backwardation and pushing up the one-month lease rates from 5.5 percent to about 12-13 percent.

But some analysts were cynical about talk of problems involving the rumoured swap saying the price rise and market tightness reflected speculation shifting to platinum from palladium as the metal could fall into "concentrated hands".
"By Monday, the price may collapse by $20," said one precious metals analyst in London.
But dealers said the tight conditions in platinum smacked of problems in getting hold of the Russian metal.
"The trouble is this situation could change....there are people who can take advantage of the situation and sell."
He said under normal circumstances, the metal was readily available, if not from Russia, from South Africa.
Players would be wary of any signs that big producer South Africa would jump in to increase supplies, dealers said.
In gold, brokers GNI said while the market was weak it could peak above $345 "to try to shake out the weak shorts."
But the market showed reluctance to jolt out of its range with any moves above $345 likely to be sold into, analysts said.

Silver was almost static at 4.72/$4.74 after a rollercoaster ride on Thursday touching both ends of its range of $4.85 and $4.65. Palladium bucked platinum's trend and slipped $3.50 on the day to $150.00/$151.50.
